title: The Blank on the Stone: Philip K. Dick from the Berkeley Record Counter to the Pink Light
register: national mythology: the canon is true

segments.name: The Twin and the Blank on the Stone

stops.name: Chicago, two children arrive six weeks early
stops.date_confidence: attested; the hospital is not named in any reachable source
stops.campa: Two children arrive in a Chicago winter six weeks before they are due. Dorothy Kindred and Joseph Edgar Dick name the boy Philip Kindred and the girl Jane Charlotte. Neither infant has the weight for it, there is not enough milk in the house, and the mother is young with nobody to show her how. The doubled self that runs through fifty years of his fiction starts in this week, which he will spend his life describing and cannot remember. The hospital is not named in any surviving record. Nobody who was in the room left an account of the delivery.
suggested_refs: Birth records for the Dick twins, Chicago, December 1928

stops.name: Riverside Cemetery, Fort Morgan: the stone with two names
stops.date_confidence: the death and the shared plot are attested; whether the surviving twin was brought to the burial is nowhere recorded
stops.campa: Jane Charlotte Dick dies at six weeks. The sources say malnutrition and disagree about everything else: a feeding error, a mother without milk, a hot water bottle, a car ride that ended too late. She goes into the Kindred plot on the dry Colorado plain, section K, block one, lot fifty-six, and the family orders a stone. The mason cuts both children's names, Jane's dates complete, Philip's birth date followed by nothing at all. The blank waits fifty-three years for its second number.
suggested_refs: The shared headstone of Jane Charlotte and Philip Kindred Dick, Riverside Cemetery, Fort Morgan
sources: Lawrence Sutin, Divine Invasions (1989), for the competing accounts of the cause

stops.name: Berkeley, the marriage ends when the transfer comes
stops.date_confidence: the divorce and the custody arrangement are attested to 1933; one source dates the family's move west to 1929 instead, and nothing reconciles the two
stops.campa: Joseph Edgar Dick works for the federal government and the government moves him to Reno. Dorothy will not go. The marriage ends, the boy goes to his mother, and he grows up in a house with one parent in it and a father reachable by appointment. Reno is four hours east over the pass and he does not go there. He is four years old. The record of it is administrative: a transfer, a decree, a custody arrangement filed in California. Nobody wrote down anything the child said about the year his father stopped living in the house.
suggested_refs: Divorce and custody filings for Dorothy Kindred Dick and Joseph Edgar Dick, 1933

stops.name: John Eaton Elementary, Washington: grades two through four
stops.date_confidence: the 1936-1938 residence and the grades are attested; the September start is inferred
stops.campa: Dorothy takes government work in Washington and brings her son east. He attends grades two through four at John Eaton Elementary in Cleveland Park, a brick school on Lowell Street. The years are 1936 to 1938, and what the city around him runs on is paper: departments, clerks, forms, transfers that move a family across a continent because a file said so. In June of 1938 mother and son go back to California. He never lives outside the state again for longer than a season.
suggested_refs: John Eaton Elementary School, 3301 Lowell Street NW, Washington, D.C.

stops.name: Berkeley, home for good
stops.date_confidence: attested to June 1938
stops.campa: Mother and son come back in June and take rooms in Berkeley. The town is a university, a hill, a fog line, and an unreasonable number of secondhand bookshops. He is nine years old. He will live in the Bay Area for the next thirty-four years, and every address he keeps until 1972, Berkeley and Point Reyes Station and San Rafael, is within an hour's drive of this one. Downtown, the newsstands carry the pulps at a dime apiece alongside the trade papers, face out, spaceships and women in helmets.
suggested_refs: The Berkeley of the late 1930s: university town, bookshops, and newsstand pulp distribution

stops.name: Berkeley, Stirring Science Stories on the rack
stops.date_confidence: the pool dated this discovery to 1940, which is impossible: the magazine's first issue is February 1941, after an announced December 1940 newsstand date that was not met
stops.campa: He picks up a pulp called Stirring Science Stories, run out of New York by Donald Wollheim on a budget that kills it after four issues. Inside are other worlds, written by men paid almost nothing a word. He is twelve. The issue announced for December 1940 never reached a rack; the first one that did is dated February 1941, and this is the one in his hand. The magazine is dead by 1942. The reading habit is not, and shortly after it he starts typing.
suggested_refs: Stirring Science Stories, ed. Donald A. Wollheim, Albing Publications, four issues 1941-1942

segments.name: Berkeley: Records, Rejection, and the Bureau

stops.name: Berkeley High School, the class of 1947
stops.date_confidence: the graduation year is attested; the month is inferred
stops.campa: He graduates from Berkeley High in the class of 1947. Ursula Kroeber, later Ursula K. Le Guin, is in the same class. Neither notices the other; she says afterwards that she has no memory of him from school, and he leaves no account of her at all. Decades later, when both are established writers and somebody points out the coincidence, they begin a correspondence that runs for years. The yearbook for the class of 1947 has both of them in it, on separate pages, under their own names.
suggested_refs: The Berkeley High School yearbook for the class of 1947

stops.name: Telegraph Avenue, the record counter
stops.date_confidence: employment from 1948 is attested; one source adds University Radio and extends the job to 1952, both unconfirmed
stops.campa: He takes work selling records on Telegraph Avenue, first at University Radio and TV Supply and then at Art Music, in the classical and opera bins. He learns the catalogue the way a priest learns a breviary: label, pressing, conductor, which Beethoven and whose. The pay is bad. Nothing about the shop suggests a writer, and the job runs on into the early fifties, long past the point where he has stopped calling it temporary. He is still behind that counter on the day the first story sells.
suggested_refs: Art Music Company, Telegraph Avenue, Berkeley, and the postwar classical record trade

stops.name: Berkeley, the first marriage
stops.date_confidence: the month of the marriage is attested; only one source places its end in November of the same year
stops.campa: He marries Jeanette Marlin in May. He is nineteen. By most accounts the marriage is over before the year is out, and almost nothing of it survives: no children, no letters in print, no anecdote anyone repeats. Only one source puts the end in November, and nothing else confirms the month. There will be four more wives after her, three children among them, and a life documented so thoroughly that biographers argue about the make of his car. About these six months there is a marriage record and a date.
suggested_refs: Marriage record of Philip K. Dick and Jeanette Marlin, Alameda County, May 1948

stops.name: Sather Gate, ten weeks at the university
stops.date_confidence: enrollment in September and withdrawal by mid-November are attested; sources give both anxiety and the compulsory ROTC requirement as the reason without choosing between them
stops.campa: He enrolls in September and signs up for history, psychology, philosophy, zoology, and German. By the middle of November he is gone. The reasons on record are anxiety and the compulsory military drill he cannot make himself perform, and the sources give both without choosing between them. He is twenty. He has walked out of the one institution that might have credentialed him and he has no other plan in hand. Ten weeks is the whole of his university education.
suggested_refs: University of California registrar records, fall term 1949

stops.name: Berkeley, marrying Kleo Apostolides
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: He marries Kleo Apostolides in June. They live on very little through the early fifties, in rented rooms where he writes every day and the rent comes off the record counter. She has left-wing friends and goes to their meetings; he goes to the post office with envelopes. The marriage runs nine years, the longest of his five. It covers the whole apprenticeship, the first story in 1951 and the first novel in 1955, and at the end of it he still cannot support himself by writing.
suggested_refs: Marriage record of Philip K. Dick and Kleo Apostolides, 14 June 1950

stops.name: Berkeley, the first story sold
stops.date_confidence: the sale is attested to 1951; the month is unrecorded, and the buyer named by one lens as The Magazine of Fantasy and Science Fiction is unconfirmed
stops.campa: At twenty-two he sells a short story called Roog. It is the first money anyone has paid him for a sentence. The month is not recorded anywhere, and the magazine that bought it is disputed. He is behind the record counter by day and at the machine at night. Within four years he publishes a novel, within twelve he has written more than twenty, and from this sale until his death he supports himself on paperbacks priced at thirty-five cents. He is almost never out of debt.
suggested_refs: Roog, Philip K. Dick's first professional sale, 1951

stops.name: Berkeley, agents at the door
stops.date_confidence: the visit and the debut novel are both attested to 1955; no month survives for either
stops.campa: Two agents of the Bureau come to the house to ask about Kleo's politics and about her friends. The questions are routine for 1955. The effect on him is not: he is twenty-six, and from here the state enters his novels as an institution that already knows your address and sends somebody pleasant to the door to confirm it. The same year Ace publishes Solar Lottery, his first novel, bound back to back with another man's book and sold for thirty-five cents.
suggested_refs: Solar Lottery (Ace Double D-103, 1955), Dick's debut novel

segments.name: Point Reyes Station: the High Castle Years

stops.name: Point Reyes Station, the house in West Marin
stops.date_confidence: attested; the daughter's birth on 25 February 1960 is likewise attested and is folded into this stop
stops.campa: He marries Anne Williams Rubinstein on the first of April and moves into her house at Point Reyes Station, in the dairy country west of the fog gap. It is the first real house he has lived in as an adult: rooms, quiet, a wife with money of her own, three stepdaughters. In February their daughter Laura Archer Dick is born. He is thirty, married for the third time, and living for the first time on somebody else's income in somebody else's town, forty miles and a coast range from Berkeley.
suggested_refs: The Rubinstein house at Point Reyes Station, Marin County

stops.name: Point Reyes Station, the mainstream novels come back
stops.date_confidence: the agency's return of the manuscripts is attested to January 1963; the Hugo for The Man in the High Castle was awarded later the same year
stops.campa: In January the Scott Meredith agency sends back the mainstream novels, the literary books he has written in parallel for ten years and cannot place anywhere. The door he wanted most closes in one parcel of returned typescript. Later the same year the science fiction he did sell, a novel about an America that lost the war and consults the I Ching about what to do next, takes the Hugo. Whether he ever stopped treating the prize as a consolation is not something the record settles.
suggested_refs: The unsold mainstream novels of the 1950s, published posthumously; The Man in the High Castle (1962)

stops.name: Point Reyes Station, the wife committed
stops.date_confidence: the committal is attested to 1963 with no month; one source wrongly compounds it with the 1964 suicide attempt and the 1965 divorce into a single 1965 event
stops.campa: He tells the neighbours that his wife is trying to kill him. On the strength of it Anne is taken out of the house and held two weeks in a psychiatric institution. She comes back. Nothing in the record settles whether he believed it, whether he needed to believe it, or what the amphetamines he is taking by the handful had to do with any of it. California in 1963 requires very little to commit a person. The Lanterman-Petris-Short Act, which will require more, is four years off.
stops.quote: Any given man sees only a tiny portion of the total truth, and very often, in fact almost perpetually, he deliberately deceives himself about that precious little fragment as well.
suggested_refs: California involuntary commitment procedure before the 1967 Lanterman-Petris-Short Act

stops.name: Point Reyes Station, the car off the road
stops.date_confidence: the divorce filing is attested to 1964 and the attempt follows it; no exact date survives, and the divorce was final in October 1965
stops.campa: He files for divorce. Some time after the filing he drives a car off the road deliberately, with a passenger beside him, and lives. No exact date survives for it. The marriage is finished in October of 1965, which is the date the histories print, and by then the house, the stepdaughters, and the whole settled arrangement of the High Castle years are behind him. He is thirty-six. Some accounts compress the committal, the crash, and the divorce into a single event in 1965; the sequence here follows the dates. The passenger is not named in any account of the crash.
suggested_refs: Marin County divorce filings, Dick v. Dick, 1964-1965

stops.name: San Rafael, marrying Nancy Hackett
stops.date_confidence: attested; the daughter's birth on 15 March 1967 is likewise attested and is folded into this stop
stops.campa: After the divorce he settles across the county in San Rafael and meets Nancy Hackett. They marry on the sixth of July, his fourth marriage, and in March their daughter Isolde Freya is born, who will later produce her father's novels for television under the name Isa Dick Hackett. He is thirty-seven. He is writing faster than any publisher can absorb, on amphetamines taken for the express purpose of keeping the rate up, and the money is still not there.
suggested_refs: Marriage record of Philip K. Dick and Nancy Hackett, 6 July 1966

stops.name: Santa Venetia, Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?
stops.date_confidence: publication is attested to 1968; the month is not recorded
stops.campa: In an unincorporated pocket of Marin with a San Rafael postal address he writes the two books that outlast the rest: Ubik, and a novel about telling the human from the manufactured, which Doubleday publishes in 1968 as Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep? Nothing in the household looks like a man at his peak. The amphetamine use is heavy, the money is short, the marriage is going. He is thirty-nine, and both books are shelved with the spaceships.
stops.quote: Everything is true. Everything anybody has ever thought.
stops.quote_source: Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep? (1968)
suggested_refs: Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep? (Doubleday, 1968); Ubik (1969)
sources: Wikipedia, 'Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?'

stops.name: Santa Venetia, the safe blown open
stops.date_confidence: attested to November 1971 with no day; two lenses wrongly place the house in San Rafael proper rather than Santa Venetia
stops.campa: Someone breaks into the house in November and blows the fireproof file open with an explosive. Papers are missing, papers are scattered across the floor, and nobody is ever charged. He will offer, in turn and sometimes in the same conversation, the theory of drug dealers, the theory of the Bureau, the theory of a political group, the theory of the federal government, and the theory that he did it himself and cannot remember doing it. The case is still open.
suggested_refs: Marin County sheriff's report on the November 1971 Santa Venetia burglary

segments.name: Vancouver: The Android and the Human

stops.name: Vancouver, the guest of honour
stops.date_confidence: the convention and the address are attested; the venue is undocumented, and one lens placed it at the University of British Columbia on no evidence
stops.campa: He flies north as guest of honour to a science fiction convention and reads a paper called The Android and the Human, which argues that the question has been posed backwards. The danger is not that machines will become people. It is that people are being manufactured into things that obey. Nancy has left. He tells the room he does not intend to go home, meets a young woman named Janis, and stays in the country. The convention is VCON 2, on the nineteenth of February. No source records the hall he stood in.
suggested_refs: The Android and the Human, address to the Vancouver science fiction convention, February 1972

stops.name: Vancouver, the overdose
stops.date_confidence: attested; the address of the room is not recorded in any reachable source
stops.campa: Five weeks later, alone in a rented room in a city where he knows almost nobody, he swallows potassium bromide meaning to die. He does not die. No source gives the address, no source says who found him, and no hospital record has been published. He is forty-three: two divorces in seven years, thirty-odd novels behind him, out of money in a foreign country with a return ticket he has not used. The date, the twenty-third of March, is the one part of it that is firmly attested.
suggested_refs: Vancouver hospital admissions, March 1972

stops.name: X-Kalay, Vancouver: the confrontation house
stops.date_confidence: entry to the program is attested to spring 1972; the facility's address is not recorded, and the confrontational-therapy description comes from the biographical tradition
stops.campa: He checks himself into X-Kalay, a residential house run by former addicts on the working principle that a man goes on lying until the room stops letting him. He arrived in this city eight weeks ago as a guest of honour. He is now a resident of a halfway house. He tells them he is an addict, which is the price of admission. He is there weeks rather than months, and he comes out of it sober enough to travel. The building's address is not recorded in anything reachable.
suggested_refs: The X-Kalay Foundation, Vancouver, and the Synanon-derived confrontation model

stops.name: California State University, Fullerton: the invitation south
stops.date_confidence: the relocation is attested to 1972; the month is inferred from the Vancouver sequence, and the arrangement of the manuscript deposit rests on the biographical tradition
stops.campa: An English professor named Willis McNelly, who teaches science fiction at a state college in Orange County and considers it literature, writes to the wrecked man in Vancouver and invites him south. He comes. What the campus supplies is what the Bay Area had stopped supplying: students who have read all of it, and a circle of younger writers called Tim Powers, K. W. Jeter, James Blaylock. The Pollak Library here ends up holding his manuscripts. Whether McNelly arranged that is not documented.
suggested_refs: The Philip K. Dick Science Fiction Collection, Pollak Library Special Collections, CSU Fullerton

stops.name: Fullerton, the shared houses
stops.date_confidence: the Fullerton household is documented in later recollections rather than records; the date is approximate and the address is not recorded
stops.campa: He lives in and around a shifting household of students and young writers in flat, hot, tract-built Orange County, a landscape of parking lots and stucco and freeway ramps that he takes personally. He is forty-four and starting again with no wife, no house, and a reputation inside the field considerably larger than his bank balance. The friends who take him in are twenty years younger than he is. What is known about this household comes almost entirely from their later recollections, not from documents.
stops.quote: Certainly it constitutes bad news if the people who agree with you are buggier than batshit.
suggested_refs: Tim Powers and K. W. Jeter on the Fullerton household, in later published recollections

stops.name: Fullerton, marrying Tessa Busby
stops.date_confidence: attested; the son's birth on 25 July 1973 is likewise attested and is folded into this stop
stops.campa: He marries Leslie Busby, called Tessa, on the eighteenth of April. She is eighteen years younger than he is. Their son Christopher Kenneth Dick is born on the twenty-fifth of July, three months after the wedding, and Dick is a father for the third time at forty-four. The apartment is small, the money is short, and the writing has slowed almost to nothing. It is the quietest year he has had since Point Reyes Station, and the address of it was never written down.
suggested_refs: Marriage record of Philip K. Dick and Leslie Busby, 18 April 1973

stops.name: Fullerton, the pink light
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: An impacted wisdom tooth comes out under sodium pentothal and the pain follows him home. The pharmacy sends a young woman with the Darvon. At the door she is wearing a gold pendant in the shape of a fish, and the low winter sun comes off it into his eyes as a beam of pink light. She tells him the sign is an old one, used by the early Christians. Then she walks back down to her car and drives off, and he is still standing in the doorway with the paper bag in his hand and the door open.
stops.quote: I experienced an invasion of my mind by a transcendentally rational mind, as if I had been insane all my life and suddenly I had become sane.
stops.quote_source: Philip K. Dick, interview with Charles Platt
suggested_refs: The ichthys, the early Christian fish sign, and its use as a recognition mark

stops.name: Fullerton, the Empire never ended
stops.date_confidence: the visions are attested to February and March 1974; their contents come from Dick's own accounts, which the sources report as such
stops.campa: Through late February and March the visions do not stop. Geometric patterns arrive in bursts, thousands of them, abstract paintings fired through the eye faster than he can name them. He sees first-century Rome laid over Orange County and a second man inside him called Thomas, a Christian in hiding from an empire Dick becomes certain never fell. A voice tells him his infant son has an undiagnosed inguinal hernia. The doctors find it and operate. He calls the source Zebra, then God, then VALIS.
suggested_refs: The 2-3-74 material as gathered in The Exegesis of Philip K. Dick (2011)

stops.name: Fullerton, the letter to the Bureau
stops.date_confidence: the letter is attested to 1974; no month is recorded, so the date defaults within the year
stops.campa: He writes to the Federal Bureau of Investigation to report that a professor of literature at San Diego and several others are foreign agents, and that the Polish novelist Stanislaw Lem does not exist, being instead a cover name for a committee working on behalf of the Communist bloc. Twenty years earlier two agents stood in his Berkeley doorway asking about his wife's friends, and he wrote a decade of fiction out of the fear it left. The month of the letter is not recorded. No reply has been published.
stops.quote: To fight the Empire is to be infected by its derangement ... Whoever defeats the Empire becomes the Empire; it proliferates like a virus ... thereby it becomes its enemies.
suggested_refs: Dick's 1974 correspondence with the FBI, in his collected letters

stops.name: Fullerton, the Exegesis begins
stops.date_confidence: the Exegesis is attested to have begun in 1974 and continued until his death; the exact starting date is not recorded
stops.campa: He begins writing it out by hand at night, on whatever paper is nearest, and does not stop for eight years: eight thousand pages, a million words, one question. He reads the Zurich psychiatrist Carl Gustav Jung on the book of Job and finds a God still being formed by the creature that suffers him. He reads Ezekiel at the canal of Chebar, the wheel with eyes in its rim, and recognizes a man handed something larger than his vocabulary. He proposes an answer, discards it, proposes the next.
stops.quote: I am a fictionalizing philosopher, not a novelist; my novel and story-writing ability is employed as a means to formulate my perception. The core of my writing is not art but truth.
stops.quote_source: In Pursuit of VALIS: Selections from the Exegesis, ed. Lawrence Sutin (1991)
suggested_refs: Carl Gustav Jung, Answer to Job (1952); the Chebar vision of Ezekiel 1

stops.name: Fullerton, Flow My Tears, the Policeman Said
stops.date_confidence: publication is attested to 1974 with no month; the John W. Campbell Memorial Award for the novel was presented in 1975, not 1974 as one lens had it
stops.campa: The novel appears in 1974, the first he has finished after a long silence. He is forty-five and back in print. Between the typing and the publication a woman came to his door with a fish around her neck, and he has begun reading his own earlier novels as reports filed in advance by somebody who already knew what was coming. The John W. Campbell Memorial Award goes to the book in the spring of 1975, honouring the previous year. A good deal of writing about him puts it in 1974.
suggested_refs: Flow My Tears, the Policeman Said (1974), winner of the 1975 John W. Campbell Memorial Award

stops.name: Fullerton, Radio Free Albemuth in the drawer
stops.date_confidence: the 1976 composition rests on the biographical tradition; publication came in 1985, three years after his death
stops.campa: He tries to put the whole thing into a novel for the first time and finds he cannot do it straight, so he splits himself in two on the page: one man who receives the transmission, and one man, a science fiction writer named Philip, who listens to him and doubts. The book does not sell. It sits in a drawer until 1985, three years after the funeral, by which point he has written a second and better version of the same story and given it another name.
suggested_refs: Radio Free Albemuth, written 1976, published 1985

segments.name: Santa Ana: the Last Six Years

stops.name: Santa Ana, the last apartment
stops.date_confidence: the move is placed in 1976 by the biographical tradition; neither the month nor the address is recorded
stops.campa: The marriage to Tessa ends and he moves a few miles down the freeway into an apartment in Santa Ana. He is forty-seven. The apartment holds a typewriter, a stereo, cats, the Exegesis in a growing stack, and a telephone he uses at three in the morning on friends who pick up. He has no wife, no house, and no settled account of what happened to him in February of 1974, though he has written several thousand pages of attempts at one. This is the address where he dies. Nobody has published the street number.
suggested_refs: Dick's Santa Ana apartment, 1976-1982; address unrecorded in published sources

stops.name: Santa Ana, A Scanner Darkly
stops.date_confidence: publication is attested to 1977; the month is not recorded
stops.campa: He publishes the book about the drug years: an undercover officer assigned to watch a suspect who turns out to be himself, in a house full of people saying brilliant and ruined things to one another. He wrote it out of the Marin and Orange County households and the people who passed through them, and he calls it afterwards the best thing he did. The author's note at the back is a list of friends with what happened to each of them set beside the name. His own name is on the list.
stops.quote: Drug misuse is not a disease, it is a decision.
suggested_refs: A Scanner Darkly (1977) and its Author's Note

stops.name: Metz, France: "If You Find This World Bad, You Should See Some of the Others"
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day; the Second Metz International Science Fiction Festival ran 19-25 September 1977 with Dick as guest of honour, the speech delivered at the city hall on the Place d'Armes, cut down twenty minutes from a longer prepared draft at the organizers' request and translated live into French from that shortened text. The reception details (Brunner, Zelazny, the room's confusion, Dick's own fondness for the trip) come from the English Wikipedia article on the speech, which does not itself footnote a primary source for the individual anecdotes
stops.campa: He crosses the Atlantic as guest of honour at the Metz science fiction festival, cutting twenty minutes at the organizers' request and reading the rest through a translator working from the wrong version. He calls it orthogonal time: a Programmer and a dark counterplayer branching worlds against each other, Christ teaching a route between them, the past itself revisable. The room goes silent, stunned; John Brunner cannot tell if he means it or if the years have worn him down, and someone decides he means to found a religion. Roger Zelazny calls the whole afternoon Dickian. Dick will remember it as the best time of his life.
stops.quote: We are living in a computer-programmed reality, and the only clue we have to it is when some variable is changed.
stops.quote_source: Philip K. Dick, question-and-answer session following "If You Find This World Bad, You Should See Some of the Others," Metz, 24 September 1977
suggested_refs: "If You Find This World Bad, You Should See Some of the Others," first published in French translation, L'année 1977-1978 de la Science-Fiction et du Fantastique (1978); English text in The Shifting Realities of Philip K. Dick (1995)
The Second Metz International Science Fiction Festival, 19-25 September 1977, John Brunner and Roger Zelazny among the attendees

stops.name: Santa Ana, VALIS
stops.date_confidence: publication is attested to 1981; the month is not recorded
stops.campa: He publishes the novel that puts his own name and his own breakdown on the page, split once more: Horselover Fat, who received the pink light, and Philip Dick, who reports on his friend Fat with clinical sympathy. Horselover is Philip in Greek, Fat is Dick in German, and the joke is the diagnosis. The cosmology underneath is Zoroaster's, light against an adversary, in Gnostic dress: an empire of iron that never ended, and something firing information into it from outside.
stops.quote: It is sometimes an appropriate response to reality to go insane.
suggested_refs: VALIS (Bantam, 1981), first volume of an unfinished trilogy

stops.name: Santa Ana, the last novel written
stops.date_confidence: the composition date is inferred; The Transmigration of Timothy Archer was published shortly after his death in 1982, making it the last novel he wrote rather than the last published in his lifetime
stops.campa: He writes one more and it is not science fiction: a novel about a California bishop who loses his son and his mistress and then goes into the desert after a scrap of first-century text, to find out whether the thing he has been preaching is true. Every question the Exegesis has been asking for eight years is in it, put by people at dinner tables in Berkeley. He finishes it and sends it off. The Transmigration of Timothy Archer is published in 1982, a few months after his death.
suggested_refs: The Transmigration of Timothy Archer (1982), published posthumously

stops.name: Santa Ana, the city they built out of his book
stops.date_confidence: the viewing is placed in early 1982 by widely repeated accounts that disagree on whether it was a screening or a videotape
stops.campa: Someone from the production brings him early effects footage of the city they have built out of his 1968 novel, a Los Angeles of rain and smoke and lit signs a hundred feet tall. The novel is fourteen years old. The accounts differ on whether he sat in a screening room or watched a tape in the apartment, and nothing available settles it. They agree on what he said, which was that it looked exactly like what he had seen. He is fifty-three. The film opens in June.
suggested_refs: Blade Runner (dir. Ridley Scott, 1982), effects test footage shown to Dick in early 1982

stops.name: Santa Ana, the call to the therapist
stops.date_confidence: attested; one lens wrongly put the stroke itself on this day, which the sources give as the day of the telephone call
stops.campa: On the seventeenth he telephones his therapist and says he cannot see properly. He had finished an interview earlier the same day. He is told to get to a hospital at once. He does not go. On the eighteenth he is found on the floor of the apartment, unconscious, after a stroke. Nobody records how long he had been lying there or what he was doing when it started. Several accounts put the stroke itself on the seventeenth and merge it with the call; the sources give the eighteenth. He is taken to hospital in Santa Ana. He does not speak again.
suggested_refs: Clinical accounts of Dick's final illness, February 1982

stops.name: Western Medical Center, Santa Ana: the machines turned off
stops.date_confidence: attested; one lens pinned the hospital 2.4 km off and wrongly described him as dying five days short of his fifty-fourth birthday, which would have fallen nine months later
stops.campa: A second stroke takes him in the hospital on the twenty-fifth of February and the brain stops. He is kept breathing while the family decides. On the second of March the machines are turned off, and Philip Kindred Dick dies at fifty-three, in a hospital on North Tustin Avenue in Santa Ana. Several accounts say he died five days short of his fifty-fourth birthday. He was born in December, so the birthday was nine months off. Blade Runner opens on the twenty-fifth of June.
stops.quote: Reality is that which when you stop believing in it, it doesn't go away.

stops.name: Riverside Cemetery, Fort Morgan: the date cut at last
stops.date_confidence: the burial beside Jane in section K, block 1, lot 56 is attested to March 1982; the exact day is not recorded
stops.campa: His ashes go back to Colorado, to section K, block one, lot fifty-six in the Kindred family plot, into the ground beside his twin. The burial is in March of 1982 and the day of it is not recorded. A mason returns to a stone cut in 1929 and fills the blank that has waited under his name for fifty-three years. Jane Charlotte Dick, six weeks old. Philip Kindred Dick, fifty-three years. The two lines are on one piece of Colorado granite, and the stone had been carrying his name since before he could read it.
